clue.text: Appliance one is content to see gathering dust in a corner?

definitions.text: Appliance one is content to see gathering dust in a corner?

parts.words: Appliance one is content to see gathering dust in a corner?
parts.note: a household machine you are glad to see sucking up dirt from a corner, rather than one left neglected and dusty there

explanation.surface: An appliance so little used that its owner is happy to let it sit forgotten in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering dust' usually means lying unused; here it means actively collecting dust, which is the appliance's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A household cleaning machine that sucks up dirt is exactly the appliance whose dust-gathering pleases its owner.

clue.text: Top dog turned first-class scrounge getting sandwich

parts.note: the top dog is the winner, the victor

indicators.note: turned means the first-class symbol is read backwards

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written AI
to sponge is to scrounge off others

explanation.surface: A dominant dog has gone over to begging for a sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: A Victoria sandwich is the British name for this jam-filled sponge cake, so 'sandwich' is a cake, not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sponge is also called a Victoria sandwich, two layers of cake with jam between.

clue.text: Clergyman accepted rule

definitions.meaning: a cathedral clergyman holding a particular office

explanation.surface: A churchman agreed to a regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cathedral cleric and an established principle or body of rules.

clue.text: Loose-jointed girl runner right away approaching style essentially like clockwork

indicators.note: loose-jointed suggests limbs flopping out of place, so the letters of girl runner are rearranged
away says the letter for right is taken out of the fodder
essentially points to the heart of the word style, its middle letter

explanation.surface: A gangly girl athlete runs with a style that is mechanical and regular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' takes one R out of GIRL RUNNER; 'Loose-jointed' rearranges the remaining nine letters, and Y, the centre of 'style', follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done like clockwork happens precisely and without fail, the sense of never going astray.

clue.text: Proper name for a fool?

definitions.meaning: a man's first name, a capitalised proper noun
British slang for a silly person

explanation.surface: Asks what the correct term would be for an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper' looks like 'correct' but means a proper noun; calling someone 'a right charlie' is British slang for calling them a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's given name and also informal British slang for a fool.

clue.text: Acclaimed cockney charm given a rest

indicators.note: cockneys traditionally drop their aitches, so the initial H of each word goes

parts.note: a hex is a spell or charm
halted means stopped, given a rest

explanation.surface: A Londoner's praised charm has been put to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cockney' removes the H from both HEX and HALTED, as a cockney would say them: 'EX 'ALTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exalted has been raised high and praised, much like being acclaimed.

clue.text: Fancy having turned up. Mike is in shock

indicators.note: is in places the letter for Mike within the reversed cake
in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a fancy is a small iced cake, a bun
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone has had a fancy turn up, and Mike is left in a state of shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone can leave them deadened and without feeling, so the verb works as the definition.

clue.text: Wine to go with beef or game

parts.note: red is wine
to beef is to complain, to grouse

explanation.surface: Choosing a red wine to go with a beef dish or with game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' and 'game' both look like food beside 'Wine', but 'beef' is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: This moorland bird is a classic British game bird, shot for sport and eaten.

clue.text: Checked sweet can bake better mixed with last of icing

indicators.note: mixed, as in a cake bowl, means these letters are rearranged
last of picks the final letter of icing

explanation.surface: Advice that a cake turns out better when finished off with icing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges CAN BAKE BETTER together with G, the last letter of 'icing'.
explanation.definitionFit: This British cake has a pink and yellow chequerboard cross-section, so it is a sweet with a checked pattern.

clue.text: Cameron confused about Northern area being part of Ireland

indicators.note: about says the scrambled name goes around the letter for Northern
confused says the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A British prime minister baffled about which region belongs to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern' tempts toward Northern Ireland, but it supplies only N; the region is in the west of the Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Connemara is a rugged region of County Galway in the west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Clairvoyant showing no sign of hesitation; instead a means of communication

indicators.note: showing no says the hesitation sound is dropped from the psychic
instead says the letter a takes the dropped letters' place

parts.note: a medium is a clairvoyant who contacts spirits
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A psychic who speaks without hesitating has become a channel of communication.
explanation.definitionFit: Press, broadcasting and similar channels are collectively the ways information reaches people.

clue.text: One charged with possession died from barbiturate

indicators.note: died from says the letter for died is taken off the drug

parts.note: a downer is a depressant drug such as a barbiturate

explanation.surface: A drug suspect charged with possession has died from barbiturates.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a police drugs story, but the definition is cryptic: the one put in charge of a possession is whoever has it.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of property is responsible for it, so the person in charge of a possession is whoever has it.

clue.text: Woodwind is less loud instrument

indicators.note: is less says the letter for loud is subtracted from the woodwind

parts.note: a flute is a woodwind instrument
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Claims a woodwind is a quieter instrument than some other.
explanation.definitionFit: This plucked stringed instrument of the Renaissance is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Leader of Boomtown Rats missing point — the rascal

indicators.note: leader of takes the opening letter of Boomtown
missing says a compass point is dropped from the rodents

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The frontman of the Irish band the Boomtown Rats lacks a point and is a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A badly behaved child or a young scamp is a little rascal.

clue.text: Surfing on domain name, one that's of its time now

indicators.note: surfing the web moves things about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Browsing online on a domain name that is up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surfing' rearranges ON DOMAIN with N into ANNODOMIN; I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in the year of the Lord', it labels dates in the present era, as opposed to BC ones.

clue.text: Dotty genuine unsophisticated young woman

indicators.note: dotty means scatty or crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained, sincere and naive young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a naive, innocent young woman, especially such a stage role.

clue.text: Official journalist always has look over Times first

parts.note: to gaze is to look
T is time, so two times are TT
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A government reporter always glances over The Times first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' and 'first' set the look and the times ahead of e'er, a poetic contraction a solver may not expect to meet as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, a writer for an official gazette, a government journalist.

clue.text: Working in tuxedo — high-class article for ladies' man

indicators.note: in places the word for working within the jacket

parts.note: DJ, dinner jacket, is the British term for a tuxedo
a machine that is on is working
U means upper-class or high-class
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Wearing a dinner jacket and a posh accessory to attract women.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Spanish seducer, his name is used for any womaniser.

clue.text: Drunk's sound of snoring interrupting only daughter

indicators.note: interrupting puts the snore inside the word for only

parts.note: sole means only
zz is the cartoon sound of snoring

explanation.surface: A drunk's snoring keeps waking his only daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is British slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Peter out with Ian on vacation in double date with loveless Leo

indicators.note: in places the pieces within the pair of date letters
double says the letter for date appears twice
on vacation empties the name, leaving only its outer letters
loveless removes O, love as a score of zero

explanation.surface: Peter and Ian go out on a double date with an unloved Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a name alongside Ian and Leo, but 'Peter out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that peters out shrinks away gradually until nothing remains.

clue.text: Language at its most basic: 'Gi's a bell!'

definitions.meaning: the smallest unit of speech sound in a language
British slang for 'give us a ring', a request to be called on the telephone

explanation.surface: A basic version of language, followed by a casual plea to be rung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give us a bell' is everyday British slang for 'phone me'; split the answer as PHONE ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguists define this as the smallest unit of sound that distinguishes words.

clue.text: Spots politician hoarding fortunes? On the contrary

indicators.note: hoarding would put fortunes inside the politician
on the contrary swaps that, so the politician sits inside the fortunes

parts.note: piles of money are fortunes
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Acne on a politician who hoards money.
explanation.definitionFit: Small inflamed blemishes on the skin are spots.

clue.text: Somewhat loathsome obscenity

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the word loathsome is used

explanation.surface: A rather nasty piece of bad language.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word, a curse, is an obscenity.

clue.text: Slick 25 perhaps

definitions.meaning: a thin layer, as of oil on water
the answer to 25 is a grand spectacular, an example of a movie

explanation.surface: A slick cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil slick is a thin film; an epic is a kind of movie.

clue.text: Ape managed to stop try going over

indicators.note: to stop means plug the gap, so the word for managed fills the reversed attempt
going over says the attempt is turned backwards

parts.note: a go is a try
ran means managed

explanation.surface: A monkey managed to halt a rugby try being scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortened form of orang-utan, the great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: A victory once more

parts.note: a gain is a win, a victory

explanation.surface: Another win, a repeated victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a second time means doing it once more.

clue.text: Ignore the odds of disco record heading to be huge

indicators.note: heading says the record comes in front

parts.note: EP, extended play, is a record

indicators.note: ignore the odds keeps only the even letters of disco

explanation.surface: Skip the odd disco record, which will go on to be enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of epic proportions is vast, heroic in scale.

clue.text: Good to ogle without yen to arouse

indicators.note: without means the yen symbol is taken away

parts.note: to eye up is to ogle
Y is the symbol for yen, the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Ogling without desire is a good way to excite someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like longing, matching the leering surface, but is the Japanese currency, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge on a horse, or to stir someone into action, is to rouse them.

clue.text: Religious leader in a part of Africa with a youngster? The opposite

indicators.note: the opposite says the whole run of pieces is written in reverse order

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a lad is a youngster

explanation.surface: A spiritual leader living in Africa with a child, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' reverses the string A MALI A LAD letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This title is held by the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: The cultivation and care of arugula could be an intellectually demanding activity

definitions.text: The cultivation and care of arugula
definitions.meaning: arugula is the salad leaf also called rocket, and its study would be its science
the proverbial hardest discipline, as in 'it's not ...'

explanation.surface: Growing salad leaves might be harder than it looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'it isn't rocket science' makes the space engineering field the byword for difficult thinking.
